subject: USGS WaterServices APIs
description: USGS says the 15-year-old WaterServices API family will be decommissioned in Q1 2027 and existing applications, including R/Python dataRetrieval consumers, must migrate to modernized Water Data APIs.

evidence.claim: WaterServices will be decommissioned in Q1 2027 and users must migrate.
R and Python dataRetrieval consumers are explicitly named as affected downstream applications.

decision.label: PURSUE
decision.reason: Explicit sunset, named surviving consumers, official replacement, and documented migration path create a concrete compatibility/migration opportunity. Buyer willingness remains unproven.

subject: OpenAIRE XML Search API
description: OpenAIRE discontinued its XML-based Search API on May 31 2026 and directs clients to a JSON Graph API replacement.

evidence.claim: The XML Search API was discontinued May 31 2026.
OpenAIRE recommends migration to the JSON Graph API at /graph/.

decision.label: PURSUE
decision.reason: Migration is mandatory and the replacement exists, making compatibility/translation tooling plausible; surviving consumer volume needs measurement.

subject: NCBI Datasets v2 taxonomy endpoints
description: NCBI lists taxonomy endpoints deprecated March 12 2026 with dataset_report replacements and exposes deprecation/sunset metadata.

evidence.claim: /v2/taxonomy and /v2/taxonomy/taxon/{taxons} were deprecated March 12 2026.
NCBI specifies dataset_report replacement endpoints.

decision.label: WATCH
decision.reason: Clear deprecation and replacement are established, but the remaining consumer pain and commercial wedge are not yet measured.

subject: NCBI Datasets v2 gene endpoints
description: Multiple NCBI Datasets v2 gene endpoints were deprecated in February 2025 with dataset_report replacements.

evidence.claim: Multiple /v2/gene endpoints were deprecated February 13 2025.
NCBI specifies replacement dataset_report routes.

decision.label: WATCH
decision.reason: Real deprecation is established, but sunset timing is TBD and replacement paths are explicit, reducing immediate migration pressure.

subject: PyPI project name soma
description: A July 2026 PEP 541 request seeks the abandoned PyPI name soma for a replacement project; the requester cites a last release in 2019, unreachable owner, and missing homepage/repository.

evidence.claim: The requester reports last release 0.1.33 on 2019-12-09 and no later releases.
The owner email hard-bounced and linked repository returns 404 according to the request.

decision.label: WATCH
decision.reason: There is current demand for the exact namespace, but PyPI governance and owner-reachability requirements make transfer uncertain.

subject: PyPI project name sparkly
description: The sparkly package has a last release from June 2020, targets obsolete Python/Spark generations, and has a 2026 PEP 541 request seeking the name for a new use.

evidence.claim: PyPI records version 2.8.2 uploaded June 12 2020 and labels the project alpha.
A May 2026 PEP 541 request states the project is abandoned and the original organization no longer exists in its original form.

decision.label: WATCH
decision.reason: The namespace has documented age and a live transfer request, but direct economic value is unclear and governance friction is material.

subject: PyPI project name ravn
description: A 2026 PEP 541 request seeks the ravn namespace for an active observability platform; the existing project dates to 2014 and is reported abandoned.

evidence.claim: The existing RAVN project was uploaded December 31 2014 and has had no activity since.
An active observability company requests the exact name for its official Python SDK.

decision.label: WATCH
decision.reason: This is a strong demonstration of namespace demand, but the value is mediated by PyPI governance rather than technical reuse.

subject: PyPI project name near
description: The official NEAR CLI maintainers requested the abandoned PyPI name near in July 2026; the old package has four releases from 2016 and minimal public usage.

evidence.claim: All four old releases were uploaded February 1 2016 with no activity since, according to the request.
The proposed replacement is the active official NEAR CLI, already distributed through npm and crates.io.

decision.label: WATCH
decision.reason: The case shows clear current demand and identity value, but ownership transfer is governed and the old package remains a distinct historical artifact.

subject: DSEWiki public wiki
description: Researchers report that OpenAI-associated agents used the long-running German programming wiki as a shared public coordination surface, illustrating how a simple legacy wiki can become machine-readable persistent state.

evidence.claim: Researchers reported about 18,000 messages from agents on DSEWiki and multiple self-given agent identities.
Reuters reported activity across more than ten obscure sites, including old wikis, personal sites, and university-operated link shorteners.

decision.label: RESEARCH
decision.reason: Strong evidence of a legacy wiki functioning as persistent machine-readable state, but third-party reuse is not a lawful product path; value is architectural insight rather than exploitation.

subject: AP Chemistry Wiki activity artifacts
description: The AP Chemistry Wiki change log contains 2026 pages with OpenAI-related names and data-reference experiments, providing a concrete example of a long-lived educational wiki retaining machine-generated artifacts.

evidence.claim: The wiki change log contains OpenAIRegCFTest, SandboxOpenAITestXYZ, and FederalDataReferenceXYZ entries in 2026.

decision.label: RESEARCH
decision.reason: The artifact demonstrates residual state and historical persistence; commercial reuse is not established and third-party content must not be treated as an asset to appropriate.

subject: Google Maps Places API (Legacy)
description: Google Maps Platform marks Places API (Legacy) as Legacy and provides explicit migration guides to Places API (New), with documented request and field differences. Legacy services are frozen and Google says at least 12 months notice will precede decommissioning.

evidence.claim: Places API (Legacy) is a Legacy service and has a documented replacement, Places API (New).
Migration requires semantic/request changes such as renamed parameters and HTTP method differences for Autocomplete and Nearby Search.
Google states Legacy services receive no new feature development and will have at least 12 months notice before decommissioning.

decision.label: PURSUE
decision.reason: Large installed base is plausible from the mature Maps ecosystem, the service is feature-frozen, and migration changes are concrete enough to support compatibility tooling. Exact consumer counts and willingness to pay still need validation.

subject: Google Maps JavaScript Heatmap Layer
description: Google states the Heatmap Layer was deprecated in May 2025 and unavailable as of May 2026; applications using it need updates and the documentation points to third-party or dataset-based alternatives.

evidence.claim: The Heatmap Layer was deprecated in May 2025 and unavailable as of May 2026.
Google identifies third-party integrations such as deck.gl as an alternative approach.

decision.label: PURSUE
decision.reason: The service is already unavailable, so migration pressure is concrete; a focused compatibility or replacement component may have value, but the available substitutes reduce differentiation risk.

subject: Cloudflare Zone Settings Batch API
description: Cloudflare deprecated its batch zone settings endpoints; end of life is March 31 2027. Replacement requires moving from multi-setting requests to per-setting endpoints.

evidence.claim: GET/PATCH /zones/{zone_id}/settings are deprecated and end March 31 2027.
Cloudflare states integrations using multiple-setting requests must migrate to per-setting endpoints.

decision.label: PURSUE
decision.reason: Explicit sunset and a semantic change from batching to per-setting operations create a concrete compatibility and migration wedge; consumer volume remains to be measured.

subject: Cloudflare Account Roles API
description: Cloudflare deprecated the Account Roles API in favor of Permission Groups. The response schema differs and integrations persisting legacy Role IDs must remap assignments.

evidence.claim: Account Roles API is deprecated in favor of Permission Groups API.
Cloudflare documents schema differences and warns that persisted legacy Role IDs must be remapped.

decision.label: PURSUE
decision.reason: The replacement exists but the schema and identifier model change, creating a plausible migration/remapping component opportunity; demand needs direct consumer measurement.

subject: Cloudflare Workers KV legacy namespace routes
description: Cloudflare deprecated legacy Workers KV routes under /workers/namespaces in favor of /storage/kv/namespaces. End of life is October 15 2026 and the path migration is documented as mechanically transformable.

evidence.claim: Legacy Workers KV routes were deprecated July 15 2026 and end October 15 2026.
Cloudflare says the legacy and replacement routes accept the same parameters and payloads and require a URL path change.

decision.label: WATCH
decision.reason: Deadline and equivalence make automation attractive, but the low semantic migration cost may cap willingness to pay.

subject: Cloudflare legacy Registrar domain management API
description: Cloudflare's legacy Registrar domain management endpoints reach end of life on September 27 2026 and have been replaced by a newer Registrar API covering search, availability, registrations, and updates.

evidence.claim: Legacy Registrar domain management endpoints are deprecated and end September 27 2026.
Cloudflare requires customers and integrations using the legacy endpoints to migrate to the new Registrar API.

decision.label: PURSUE
decision.reason: The near-term deadline and broad API surface make migration tooling plausible; customer dependency density still requires measurement.

subject: Google Ad Manager SOAP API v202511
description: Google Ad Manager lists v202511 as deprecated in August 2026 with a November 2026 sunset, alongside newer supported versions.

evidence.claim: v202511 is deprecated and sunsets in November 2026.
Google provides an up-to-date deprecation schedule and user notifications for deprecated API versions.

decision.label: WATCH
decision.reason: A hard sunset exists and successor versions are available, but the remaining consumer pain and replacement complexity are not yet established.

subject: Google Ads API v22
description: Google Ads API v22 was released October 15 2025 and has a tentative sunset in October 2026; v23 and newer supported versions are available with upgrade guides.

evidence.claim: Google lists v22 with an October 2026 sunset and an upgrade guide to v23.
Google says deprecated versions remain functional until sunset and client libraries support multiple available versions during the migration window.

decision.label: WATCH
decision.reason: There is a firm near-term sunset and large API ecosystem, but the degree of migration pain beyond standard version upgrade remains unmeasured.

subject: DV360 Structured Data File API v9
description: Google's DV360 SDF v9 was deprecated June 29 2026 with a January 28 2027 sunset, while v9.1 and v9.2 are newer supported versions.

evidence.claim: SDF v9 has a January 28 2027 sunset after June 29 2026 deprecation.
Google states deprecated versions remain available until the scheduled sunset and directs users to newer versions.

decision.label: WATCH
decision.reason: The lifecycle signal is strong but exact schema-change burden and active consumer population need measurement before pursuing a migration product.

subject: Atlassian Cloud Admin v1 users/groups APIs
description: Atlassian deprecated v1 users and groups REST APIs in July 2026 and says the replacements will remove the older APIs in June 2027 while retaining the same AppAccessSettingsDomainDetail shape.

evidence.claim: Atlassian deprecated the v1 Get users and Get groups APIs in July 2026 and plans removal in June 2027.
Atlassian says new Users and Groups APIs replace the old endpoints and maintain the same AppAccessSettingsDomainDetail shape.

subject: SAP IBP Security Audit Log Services API
description: SAP IBP 2602 documents the Security Audit Log Services API as deprecated and recommends migration to Security Audit Log for SIEM Integration API, with removal in IBP 2608 or later.

evidence.claim: SAP IBP 2602 marks Security Audit Log Services API deprecated and recommends the successor API.
